summary.headline: Netweb Q2 FY27 revenue rose 335.7% YoY to INR1,323 crores and PAT to INR137 crores, with an order book of INR2,629 crores.
summary.overview: Netweb reported a record Q2 FY27 with revenue from operations of INR1,323 crores (up 335.7% YoY, up 61.4% QoQ), operating EBITDA of INR197 crores at a 14.9% margin, and PAT of INR137 crores at a 10.2% margin. H1 FY27 PAT of INR222 crores already exceeded full-year FY26 PAT of INR206 crores. The company raised INR1,200 crores through a QIP, moved to zero net debt with net cash of INR14 crores, and reported an order book of INR2,629 crores plus L1 of INR653 crores. Management flagged gross margin pressure from component prices, higher inventory days (117) and a cash conversion cycle of 94 days, and guided to INR4,000 crores revenue for FY27.

guidance_outlook: Management is targeting revenue of INR4,000 crores for FY27.
Management expects 30-40% CAGR growth for the next 2-3 years, though the Sethi/Nishita questions on conservatism were not directly answered beyond reiterating the guidance.
Operating EBITDA margin is framed around 13-14% on a full-year basis; H1 slightly exceeded this range, but management said not to extrapolate it to the full year.
Cash conversion cycle expected to operate in a 90-110 day range going forward.
Vera Rubin based systems: first system to be set up in India soon, with commercial offering targeted from January; timelines could be pulled in.
Taiwan wholly owned subsidiary approved by the Board, purely for R&D, to hire design engineers locally in Taiwan.
NSM 2.0: management aims for more than half of the outlay over a 5-year program, with orders expected to come gradually.
capex_capacity: Inventory of about INR1,900 crores held to support the order book; management said it will churn into revenue in Q3 and Q4.
Standard execution timeline for orders is 10 to 16 weeks.
Taiwan wholly owned subsidiary approved for R&D; no partnership involved.
Quantum simulator and emulator R&D commenced; physical AI capabilities being developed, with no quantified timelines.
demand_pricing: Active pipeline of about INR11,152 crores; management cites about 60% conversion of pipeline into orders.
Order book rose to INR2,629 crores from about INR2,500 crores last quarter, after billing of about INR1,300 crores.
Order sizes range from about INR5 crores to about INR1,000 crores.
Government and enterprise demand both described as strong; enterprise currently seen as slightly larger than government in the pipeline.
Added 449 new customers in H1 FY27; management says new customers account for 8-9% of the revenue book.
Gross margin fell QoQ due to component price increases and deal mix; management pointed to EBITDA as the guided metric.
Memory prices have risen by 200% or more; management said this has not dampened demand.

qa_highlights.question: Gross margin decline and the steady-state base going forward?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said gross margin is best judged on a full-year basis because large-deal mix drives it; EBITDA margin was kept around 14% due to operating leverage on large deals.

qa_highlights.question: Is the order book driven by Neocloud players and the C-DAC GPU RFP?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said named customers are in the order book and funnel but did not disclose order quantities; order book grew to INR2,600 crores plus L1 of about INR3,100-3,200 crores.

qa_highlights.question: Working capital: will the cash conversion cycle normalise?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided to a 90-110 day cash conversion cycle; FY26 was 84 days, with the increase due to inventory build for the large order book.

qa_highlights.question: Can FY28+ growth of 30-35% be supported by pipeline conversion?
qa_highlights.answer: Management reiterated 30-40% CAGR for 2-3 years, citing about 60% pipeline conversion and a pipeline growing steadily; the company is not providing a conversion number for FY27 year-end.

qa_highlights.question: Will the C-DAC/India AI GPU RFP translate into orders?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the fresh India AI RFP is a request for empanelment of CSPs at market GPU rates, and orders would follow as CSPs place them with Netweb; the company is already serving many of these CSPs.

qa_highlights.question: Explain the difference between free cash in the presentation and the balance sheet cash figure.
qa_highlights.answer: Management said the gap is mainly the unutilised QIP money (about INR400 crores) and some bank guarantees and deposits, which are classified outside cash and cash equivalents.

risks_watch: Gross margin compression from component and memory price increases, and from deal mix in large orders.
Inventory of about INR1,900 crores and 117 inventory days, with working capital pressure if orders slip.
Customer concentration: management says top 5 and top 10 customers churn, but the concentration figures were not disclosed in detail.
Execution of INR2,629 crores order book and INR4,000 crores FY27 revenue target in H2 after the strategic order is largely executed.
Rising global cost of capital could affect hyperscaler capex; management said demand has not been impacted so far.
Vera Rubin launch timing (commercial sales from January) and NSM 2.0 order timing.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and growth, with repeated emphasis on record results and the pipeline. Evasive on specifics: declined to share order breakdowns, customer volumes, quantified physical AI/quantum opportunity, or a guidance refinement; gross margin questions were redirected to EBITDA.
key_quotes: Both revenue and profit grew 4x year -on-year.
As on September 30, 2026, our order book stood at INR2,629 crores with an additional L1 position of INR653 crores, providing strong revenue visibility for the coming quarters.
So basically, I leave that calculation on your end, but I can only assure you one thing that we are targeting to achieve INR4,000 crores of revenue this particular financial year.
Primarily, the Taiwan subsidiary will be only used for R&D purposes.

growth.why: Management targets INR4,000 crore FY27 revenue (vs H1 FY27 of INR2,143 crore, implying a steep H2 ramp) and 30-40% CAGR for 2-3 years, backed by a INR2,629 crore order book plus INR653 crore L1 and about INR1,900 crore of inventory to churn into Q3-Q4 revenue, but no new productive capacity was announced and the brief notes management did not directly answer questions on conservatism.
